text:
sec-bot: ALERT: [runtime-detect] Suspicious DaemonSet created in prod: 'node-proxy' (hostPID=true, privileged=true). Observed on cluster: prod-us-west-2. :rotating_light:

alex: seeing the alert, on it. which nodes flipped?

sarah: I can already see a new ClusterRoleBinding 'node-ops-crb' created 4m ago. suspicious serviceAccount: 'node-ops' in 'infra' ns. :eyes:

jordan: paste of kubectl get ds -n kube-system node-proxy -o yaml (sanitized):
```
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: DaemonSet
metadata:
  name: node-proxy
  namespace: kube-system
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      hostPID: true
      containers:
      - name: proxy
        image: docker.io/unknown/rev-proxy@sha256:4a7f...
        securityContext:
          privileged: true
```

alex: that image digest isn't in our allowlist. no cosign signature found in our registry.

lisa_ops: nodes showing pods: node-5, node-7, node-9. pod started ~2026-03-20T09:02Z. I already ran `kubectl logs` but it exits quickly. suspecting host namespace access.

oncall-mike: cordoning and isolating affected nodes now: `kubectl cordon node-5 node-7 node-9` ; also creating taint to avoid schedule. Will keep them live for forensic snapshot.

alex: good. do NOT drain yet; we need ephemeral files and host PID state. take `kubectl exec -it --namespace kube-system <pod> -- nsenter -t 1 -m -u -n -i /bin/sh` logs if possible (read-only where possible).

sarah: looking at audit logs — there was a kubectl exec from ip 18.219.11.45 using a token for serviceaccount 'node-ops' at 09:00:12Z followed by `kubectl create -f` for the daemonset. Access came from a CI runner IP (github actions runner).

jordan: checking CI metadata: workflow 'infra/auto-deploy' triggered 09:00. The runner used a long-lived secret stored in KMS key: projects/redwood/keys/infra-deploy. KMS logs show an unrecognized principal used the decrypt endpoint 09:00:05Z.

alex: possible exfil or leaked deploy key. rotate KMS key and revoke the infra-deploy key immediately. Sarah, can you revoke RBAC and SA tokens?

sarah: done: deleted ClusterRoleBinding 'node-ops-crb' and removed 'node-ops' SA tokens 09:12Z. Also created emergency RoleBinding revocation PR for the infra namespace.

lisa_ops: deleted the DaemonSet (kept a copy of yaml). PID namespace access stopped on nodes. Continuing forensic snapshots and copying /var/log/messages and container runtime logs to the forensics bucket (write-only).

oncall-mike: memory snapshot and docker/CRI logs archived to s3://redwood-forensics/inc-2026-042/ with restricted ACL.

jordan: initial triage: attacker used leaked long-lived KMS-wrapped secret from CI runner to impersonate infra deploy principal. That allowed `kubectl` usage and creation of privileged daemonset. Image appears to be a slightly modified upstream proxy with a reverse shell.

alex: coordinate comms: product/security/legal. We'll open an incident channel and page infra oncall. Also notify customers if any data plane access happened. At minimum, create incident ticket INC-2026-042.

sarah: creating incident ticket now. summary: privileged daemonset created via compromised CI credentials; contained by revocation, daemonset deletion, node isolation, forensics.

sec-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-042. PagerDuty: paged infra, security, customer-ops.

lisa_ops: quick checklist next: 1) rotate all CI deploy keys 2) rotate KMS keys 3) audit other long-lived SA tokens 4) add short-lived tokens to workflows 5) scan registries for image digest 4a7f...

jordan: registry scan returned: image pulled from docker.io/unknown/rev-proxy@sha256:4a7f... three pulls in last 24h from our prod nodes. No presence in our ECR. Looks like attacker pushed to docker hub.

alex: immediate mitigations pushed: temporary admission webhook to block hostPID/privileged in prod, and deny new DaemonSet creations in kube-system without explicit approval.

sarah: I've added audit rule that alerts on: create daemonset OR clusterrolebinding OR clusterrole creation in prod clusters. Hooked to sec-bot.

oncall-mike: rotating KMS key now. Will also rotate the service account keys and revoke GitHub App tokens that can access infra secrets. Expect remediation window ~45m.

jordan: post-incident actions proposed: - enforce image signature verification (cosign) for all cluster images - gate CI runner network egress - require short-lived service account tokens (Workload Identity/OIDC) - add OPA/Gatekeeper policy to ban hostPID/privileged by default - enhance audit retention for kube-apiserver to 90d - add automated detection for sudden new clusterrolebindings

lisa_ops: scheduling a postmortem meeting tomorrow 11:00 PT. I will attach forensic artifacts and sanitized timeline to INC-2026-042.

alex: good. customer comms draft: brief, no technical detail, note: contained, no evidence of customer data exfil so far, under investigation. Legal to review.

sarah: note to infra: remove long-lived KMS-wrapped secrets from workflows. Use ephemeral tokens or OIDC.

jordan: sec finding: our image signing enforcement is not enabled in prod due to a misconfigured admission controller. Adding remediation ticket RN-PR-556.

oncall-mike: all affected nodes still isolated but stable. No secondary persistence detected in nodes beyond the daemonset.

alex: next steps assigned: 1) forensic report (jordan, lisa_ops) 2) rotate keys & tokens (oncall-mike, sarah) 3) admission controller & policy changes (alex) 4) customer/legal comms (product + legal) 5) postmortem doc + timeline (everyone).

sarah: marking this thread as incident channel seed. Will mirror to #incidents and #eng-sre once legal ok. :white_check_mark:

sec-bot: Closing containment loop: no new detections for 30m. Monitoring on high.

alex: thanks everyone. Blameless postmortem and follow-through required.
